name: Spatial Sound
description: Walk through a delicate mechanical instrument. Gears, a pendulum, pulleys and linkages compose spatial sound from their own movement.

assets.credit: Original listening-room engraving · Tampa Curated. All sound is procedural synthesis; no audio samples.

compatibility: Modern Chrome, Firefox, Safari and Edge with SVG and Web Audio. No WebGL, runtime dependencies, remote assets or microphone access.
The context is created only after Enable sound. Device/browser audio interruptions may require pressing Mute, then Enable sound again. The room remains usable silently.
Recording uses MediaRecorder with a runtime codec check. Available formats vary; score JSON export remains available without recording support.
Keyboard, pointer and touch navigation; reduced motion starts paused. Hidden or offscreen studies stop transport and voices. Disposal closes the owned AudioContext.
notes: This is an original imaginary mechanical listening room, rendered as perspective SVG linework. The listening point and visual viewpoint share coordinates; the camera faces the back wall.

Tooth crossings trigger wood-like filtered ticks; pendulum center crossings ring a gentle tone. Half-turns of the harmonic wheel choose notes in the selected scale. Rope travel makes filtered grain and the arm plucks a muted string. Manual operation advances these same mechanical phases.
Positional sources use HRTF panning and inverse-distance attenuation. Spatialization blends that field with centered mono. Source checkboxes mute voices while their mechanisms remain visible.
Audio starts muted on every visit and in every export. Presets never carry audio activation. Master gain is capped at 60%, voices have soft envelopes, a bounded voice count and a compressor.

Stop all mutes and freezes the room. Enable sound is a deliberate restart; Run mechanisms resumes silently after Stop all. Automatic transport pauses with the Lab lifecycle; returning resumes only a previously enabled instrument.

Record up to 15 seconds of the synthesized output, preview it, or save it locally. No microphone, uploads or accounts. Pausing or muting ends a recording. Score JSON retains the most recent 256 semantic actions and exact synthesized strikes.
reuse: Serve the exported source folder over HTTP and open example.html. Everything required is local and MIT licensed. No installation or audio assets are needed.
Use createSpatialAudio independently: register positioned source IDs, enable in a user gesture, set the listener, then strike sources from your application’s actual state.
The pure mechanical transport, procedural voice generator, SVG illustration and complete demo UI are separate modules. The README documents their APIs and coordinate system.

Mount the complete room with mount(host, settings, report), call setRunning for visibility, update settings, and dispose before removing it. The source archive includes the current validated settings; it never enables audio automatically.
